Apple has updated the privacy policy for the Apple Store app, adding provisions for an upcoming virtual shopping assistant. Details below.

Apple is expanding AI use across its retail operations.

As discovered by MacRumors, the Apple Store app and its privacy page now include a new section titled "Virtual Shopping Assistant," which reads:

In other words, the Apple Store app may soon add a chatbot that uses user data to tailor responses and help users make purchasing decisions.

Apple says it will strip identifying information before sharing conversation contents with unnamed partners that provide responses for the chatbot, an approach that suggests at least part of the experience will be backed by third-party models from external companies.

Chat logs will be kept within the app so users can revisit them, while Apple will also retain them for business analytics. Users can use a new "Chat Improvements" setting to independently opt in or out of allowing their conversations to be used to improve the virtual shopping assistant.

The wording of Apple's privacy policy suggests the virtual assistant will initially be available in only a limited number of countries and regions, likely debuting in English-speaking markets before gradually expanding to more languages and regions.

This news comes months after Apple added an AI chatbot to a "Sales Coach" app, which provides sales and technical resources for the company's retail partners. Users can access the chatbot through an "Ask" tab, and it answers questions based on Apple's official training materials and documentation.

This news also comes ahead of a Bloomberg report saying Apple is testing a system called "Live Notes" at select retail stores. The system uses AI to record, transcribe and summarise Genius Bar service sessions, allowing employees to focus on helping customers without having to multitask on note-taking.
